after: ## What the specification is asking for
alt: Three rows using Musa (AS) as the example: life is the main events in order; role is the job Allah gave him, messenger and receiver of the Tawrat; importance is what Muslims learn today, such as courage against tyranny and trust in Allah.
caption: Retelling the life does not answer a question about importance.

after: ## Adam (AS): the first human and the first prophet
alt: Five steps in the life of Adam (AS): Allah announces a khalifah, Adam is created from clay and taught the names, Iblis refuses out of pride, Adam and his wife slip and are sent to earth, and their repentance is accepted. Below, his importance: mercy, no inherited sin, stewardship, the danger of pride and equality.
caption: Adam’s forgiven mistake teaches that sincere repentance is always accepted.

alt: Six events from the life of Ibraheem (AS): reasoning against worship of the stars, breaking the idols, the fire made cool, leaving Hajar and Isma’il (AS) in Makkah, the dream of sacrifice and raising the Ka’aba. Below, how worship recalls him: Sa’i remembers Hajar, the Eid-ul-Adha sacrifice remembers the ram, and the Ka’aba is the house he built.
caption: Hajj and Eid-ul-Adha relive Ibraheem’s submission every year.

after: ## Musa (AS): the prophet who spoke with Allah
alt: Six steps in the life of Musa (AS): saved as a baby, life in Madyan, the call at Tuwa with the signs, confronting Pharaoh with Harun (AS), the parting of the sea, and receiving the Tawrat. A note links the story to fasting on Ashura.
caption: Musa (AS) teaches courage against injustice and trust in Allah.

after: ## Isa (AS): the Messiah, son of Maryam
alt: Six Islamic beliefs about Isa (AS): his miraculous birth to Maryam, speaking from the cradle as the servant of Allah, miracles by Allah’s permission, the Injil, that he was not crucified but raised up by Allah, and his announcement of a messenger named Ahmad.
caption: Use the Islamic belief: a prophet and servant of Allah, not divine.

alt: A table of the four prophets with their title or role, book and key importance: Adam (AS), first prophet and khalifah; Ibraheem (AS), Khalilullah, given the Suhuf; Musa (AS), Kalimullah, given the Tawrat; Isa (AS), the Messiah, given the Injil. A note says the Zabur went to Dawud (AS).
caption: Suhuf with Ibraheem, Tawrat with Musa, Injil with Isa (AS).

alt: The structure of a 6-mark answer: two separate reasons, a model of Tawhid and the link to Hajj and Eid-ul-Adha, each developed with an event for 4 marks, then a source, Qur’an 4:125, quoted and applied for 2 marks.
caption: Two developed reasons plus one source applied to the question.
